title: Export delivery receipt
description: One attempt to deliver one export manifest's bundle to one sink. Returned by `deliver(manifest, bundle)` and recorded by the projector; a retry is a new attempt with a new receipt, never an edit of an old one. The ordering pair (generation, options_revision) is carried so a receipt says which material this attempt was about: a sink that already accepted a higher pair reports `skipped_superseded` instead of overwriting. The status records what is known about the attempt's effect on the sink, not the transport symptom: once a request may have been applied and no authoritative acknowledgement or refusal establishes its result, the attempt is `outcome_unknown` and must be reconciled — it is never read as delivered, never as failed, and never as a zero anywhere. What counts as authoritative is defined per adapter (docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §5).

invocation_id.description: The invocation this delivery ran under, so one id threads the chain to the commit receipt (H-1).

status.description: delivered: the sink authoritatively acknowledged the whole bundle as applied, tombstones included (for webhook_http, only the receiver protocol's applied or already_applied answer; a request accepted for later processing is not applied) — on an equal-pair replay, from its retained evidence that this same manifest and bundle content hash were already applied (docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §3). failed: the attempt's effect on the sink is established and the bundle was not delivered — nothing was applied (the request was never sent, or the sink authoritatively refused it), or the sink reported the part it did apply (`partial_write`). skipped_superseded: the sink already holds a higher ordering pair, so this attempt correctly wrote nothing. outcome_unknown: the request may have been applied and nothing authoritative establishes whether — the process stopped after sending, no response came, the response could not be read, or it was neither an acknowledgement nor a refusal. It needs reconciliation before anything may be concluded from it, and its diagnostic is `unknown_cause`, not an error class.

written.description: How much of the bundle the sink took, as an observed count. A `partial_write` failure reports `partial` with what the sink said it wrote, which is a lower bound and never a total; every other failure applied nothing, so its count is an observed zero, and so is a deliberately skipped delivery's — those are the legitimate zeros. An unknown outcome reports `unknown` (or `partial`, when some writes are known and the rest are not).

error_class.description: A typed class for a settled failure, not a message; every class names a known effect. unreachable: the request was never sent (name resolution, a refused connection, TLS setup). auth_failed: the sink authoritatively refused the credential. refused: the sink authoritatively refused the payload. schema_mismatch: the destination does not match the export schema version, and nothing was applied. quota: the sink authoritatively refused for quota or rate. timeout: the attempt timed out before any of the request was sent, or before a transaction was committed, so nothing was applied. conflict: the sink already holds different content under this same ordering pair, so it wrote nothing (docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §3). partial_write: the sink reported the part it applied before it stopped. A cause that leaves the effect unknown — an unreadable response, a timeout after sending — is never a class here: that attempt is outcome_unknown, with its unknown_cause.

unknown_cause.description: Why the outcome is unknown: the diagnostic an unknown outcome keeps instead of an error class, which would claim a settled result (Astra 0c review A2). terminated_after_send: the delivering process stopped after the request, commit or rename was issued and before its result was read. no_response_after_send: the connection closed or timed out after the request was sent, before any response. unreadable_response: a response arrived but could not be read as one. unauthoritative_response: a response was read that is neither an acknowledgement nor a refusal as the adapter defines them (for webhook_http, docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §5.3: a 202 or any other 2xx that is not the receiver protocol's applied or already_applied answer, since a queued request is not an applied one; a 200 or 409 whose Export-Webhook-Result header is missing or does not match; a 4xx the protocol does not list as a refusal; a 3xx, which is never followed; or a 5xx).

capability_fact_id.description: The dated capability fact this failure raised (`capability_facts.fact_id`). Required for a failure and for an unknown outcome: a dead export sink is a visible, dated incident with a since-time, which is the rule the 2026-09-21..24 secrets outage produced (H-2). It is never, by itself, a reason to block completion.

hold_id.description: The typed hold that owns getting this delivery finished, when one was raised (H-3: class, owner, deadline and what clears it live on the hold, not here).

allOf.description: Delivered means the sink said so: an acknowledgement time, the tombstones acknowledged, an observed count, no error and nothing left to reconcile.
A failure names its class and raises a dated capability fact; it has no acknowledgement time. It is a settled result, so its count is known.
A partial write reports the part the sink applied as a partial count: a lower bound, never an observed total (Astra 0c review A4).

Every other failure is settled because nothing was applied, so its count is an observed zero. A count that is not known means the request may have been applied: that is outcome_unknown, not a failure (Astra 0c review A2).
An unknown outcome must be reconciled, and may not claim a count it cannot know (L-4, RG-4). It is not a failure, so it does not carry an error class; it says why it is unknown in unknown_cause.
A skipped delivery is the one place a zero is knowledge: nothing was written, and that is observed, not unknown.
An unknown cause belongs only to an unknown outcome: a settled result says what happened in its status and error class.
Reconciliation is only ever pending for an unknown outcome; a known result is not quietly left open.
